text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, giving back some of the gains from earlier in the week. The decline comes as crude oil prices pulled back—U.S. oil dropped to $91.48 per barrel from the $96+ range seen globally—and broader geopolitical headlines shifted focus. While conflicts in Ukraine and Iran continue to disrupt refinery capacity and push diesel prices higher, the immediate driver today appears to be profit-taking after the stock rallied over 4% from late August through early September.

The longer context here is tension between two forces: supply-side pressures from refinery shutdowns in Russia and potential Iran production losses that support energy prices, versus signs that escalating sanctions and military involvement (South Korea now weighing action at the Strait of Hormuz) may be pricing in either resolution of those conflicts or hedging bets on oil demand if regional instability deepens further. For a refiner and upstream producer like ConocoPhillips, the benefit of higher crude prices can be offset by uncertainty about where geopolitical risk resolves.
